findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

The backup probe thermometer is stored in a pan mixed in with scrapers used for the chicken baking equipment. This poses a possible contamination source for the food contact parts of the probe thermometer and this practice should cease moving forward. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they had the probe sanitized and moved to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored so that they remain clean/sanitized prior to use.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Multiple knives are being stored between the knife rack and the wall. The wall is visibly discolored and possibly soiled around the knife rack and behind it. This is not a clean location for food contact surfaces to be in contact with while in storage. The PIC was shown and tthe situation discussed. The knives were move to dish for re-cleaning and should not be stored here moving forward. Ensure all food contact surfaces are stored in a clean location after cleaning and before use.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observed to change gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted to correct and the PIC is instructed to ensure that hand washing takes place at all times that it is required.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor.

Multiple trays of cleaned utensils are stored in plastic tubs on shelves in the kitchen area. These tubs are observed with standing water and a slimy substance in them that is in contact with the utensils. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. The utensils were moved to dish for re-cleaning and the tubs replaced during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all cleaned utensils are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times until use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

1) The floor under shelves on both sides of the walk in cooler are in need of mopping. 2) The wall near the floor in the walk in cooler appears to have mold growth developing. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean at all times.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

The hand sink to the far right in the deli area (behind the end display cooler) is observed without hand soap during this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and a new container installed during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The open top cooler on the deli floor has numerous packages of meat and cheese with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-48F. All items of concern were discarded during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

The open top cooler on the floor is not holding meats and cheeses at sufficient temperature for safety. The items noted out of temperature have been discarded, but the cooler needs to be brought into compliance. Follow up in 2 weeks to ensure the equipment is properly functioning.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Multiple employees are observed to either change gloves or put on gloves without hand washing. Education conducted and the PIC should ensure that safe hand washing practices are taking place in the food handler/ preparation areas.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Multiple items in the island cooler observed with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-48F. Items include calzones, sandwiches, salads and subs. Through investigation it appears that any foods on the bottom shelf should not be stacked more than 2 high. Also, items on the ends should be placed so that air may flow from the back of the cooler and effectively maintain the front layer of foods in safe temperatures. Foods in these areas as well as the ones probed were discarded to correct the violation.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in the customer display reach in cooler observed out of temperature. Shredded rotisserie pork observed at 50F. Product was stacked 4 containers high in the bottom of the cooler. Packages lower (closer to the bottom) were observed at 41F or below. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC and staff. Employee removed top layer and checked internal temperature of remaining packages. Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Review stocking procedures with all staff so that product is not stacked too high.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Three containers of sushi observed labeled use by 6/7. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC. Out of date foods removed from sale to be voluntarily discarded. PIC instructed employees to check the whole cooler for expired foods.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Sandwiches in the island cooler observed to be 45 to 50F. CORRECTED— Discussed with PIC. Sandwiches removed to be rapidly chilled or voluntarily discarded. Sandwiches appeared to be stocked too far to the front of the cooler, preventing them from being kept at 41F or below. Food closer to the back of the shelves observed 41F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Red buckets under the slicers observed with 0ppm quat. CORRECTED- Bucket was emptied and refilled from the wall-mounted dispenser to the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label. (Pf)

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
Time as a control is used on hot foods for service (mac & cheese, mashed potatoes, various chickens, etc). All items were observed without time markings indicating when they were removed from temperature control or when they were to be discarded. CORRECTED— Foods were observed to be 135F or above. Staff were confident that foods were removed from temperature control at 1:30, and labeled items accordingly.
3-501.19: (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Red bucket behind the deli observed with 0ppm quat. CORRECTED- Bucket was emptied and refilled from the wall-mounted dispenser to the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label. (Pf)

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Knives observed stored in the gap between the knife rack and the wall. CORRECTED-- Knives removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Knives will be stored in a clean location.
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment: Items in the hot case were removed from temperature control over 4 hours before inspection. Foods had not been used or discarded within 4 hours after being removed from temperature control. CORRECTED- Foods where time as a control was used improperly (past 4 hours) were discarded, including BBQ chicken, General Tso's chicken, wings, and tenders. Time as a Control policy documentation was provided to SCDPH during the inspection.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours (3) The FOOD shall be cooked and served, served at any temperature if READY-TO-EAT, or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature
control. (P)

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140 - Two cold cases were observed with digital thermometers that were not working properly. One did not show a readout at all. The other didn't have a readout, then it came on and went off again. Get the thermometers repaired or replaced. Provide additional thermometers to monitor the temperature of the cold salad case and cheese deli case until the built-in thermometers are repaired.

All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Sanitizer spray bottle used in the front deli area was at 0ppm quat. Associate stated it was filled this morning at ~8a. The solution coming directly out of the dispenser was also observed at 0ppm. Chemical was not pulling through the line properly. A call for service was made to get the dispenser repaired. In the meantime, the sanitizer pouch was removed from the wall mounted dispenser for solutions to be mixed by hand. Manager hand mixed a new solution for the spray bottled used in the front deli area (~300ppm).
A previously existing bottle back by the 3 part sink made at a different time was observed at ~200ppm.
Use test strips when solutions are prepared to verify they are at the proper effective concentration range of 150-400ppm.

To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.
Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Plastic storage containers in back cook/prep area were observed with buildup of splash and food debris in the bottom. Outer surfaces had a thin layer of grease accumulation as well. Clean and sanitize the utensil storage containers daily/as needed, and maintain them clean.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Handsink in back by side prep/storage area was blocked by a garbage can.
Also, two of the front area handsinks were not stocked properly. Handsink at the far end of the cold cases was without paper towels. Handsink at the far end of the hot food service area was without soap and paper towels. Soap and paper towels were provided during the inspection.

All handsinks are to be accessible at all times and have a supply of soap and paper towels to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed fried chicken in the hot case to be at temperatures (probed) between 110-120F. After further inspection of the hot case, it was noted that the other areas were maintaining proper temperatutes. The top shelf held items that are discarded at the 4 hour mark for quality. The bottom shelf is where the fried chicken was. Management discussed switching these two to ensure that chicken is continuously held at proper temperature and the other items will be in compliance since they are discarded at the four hour mark. The chicken that was in the case was marked for destruction after 5:15 PM. 
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed rotisserie chicken (1.75 hours cooling, freezer, 78-84F), buffalo chicken wings (1.5 hours cooling, cooler, 104F probed), and fried chicken (1.5 hours cooling, cooler, 80-84F probed) cooling within the walk-in cooler and freezer. The store voluntarily destroyed all of the buffalo chicken wings at the 1.5 hour mark because management did not believe it would cool quick enough. The fried chicken, except for the breasts (75F), cooled to the 70F. The breasts were destroyed. Rotisserie chicken was uncovered and attempted to cool. The final temperature was 75F at 2 hours. They were destroyed because management did not want to reheat due to issues with quality. Ensure that PHFs that are cooling are cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours and then 70 to 41F or below in 4 more hours. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
Observed an employee walk from the service line to the back with a pair of gloves on, retrieve a piece of chicken from the fryer basket with her hands, and then break it open to "check to see if it was done." Ensure that if an employee is task switching, then they are to remove the soiled gloves, wash their hands, and then don a new pair of gloves. 
750-160(b) Gloves shall be single use and used for only 1 task.  Gloves shall be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interuption in operations.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed the hot holding case to be holding at a temperature of 120F. Chicken tenders within the case were at 126F when probed. The staff were unsure as to what time each item came out to the hot holding case. The co-manager of the store had employees discard all items that had not been cooked in the last hour and started a 4 hour Time as Control Plan for all other items that had come out in the past hour. Ensure that all items are held at 135F or above when practicing hot holding. 
750-150(b)  Hot potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 135°F or above except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135°F or above. (Except for rare roast beef which may be held at 130F.)

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee was observed washing hands between tasks but did not use proper technique; hands were quickly rinsed and not washed for a full 20 seconds. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with the employee and management. Employee washed hands with proper technique prior to continuing with food prep.

Employees must properly wash hands any time they may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment and unwrapped single service articles. 
Hands must be lathered with soap for 20 seconds prior to rinsing and drying with paper towels.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Floor fans blowing in food prep areas were soiled with dust buildup.

Clean and sanitize surfaces of fans used in food prep and dish areas as needed to eliminate buildup of dust/debris that could be made airborne when fan is in-use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) label storage tubs in back prep area (splash/crumbs);
B) storage areas of metal prep tables (splash/crumbs) - time for detail cleaning;    and
C) around motor under fryer (grease buildup).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Water source safe, hot, and cooled under pressure
findings.comment: Water in most hand sinks in the deli is between 110F and 122F.  The water temperature makes it uncomfortable for employee hand washing. 750-1120 Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.  Make sure that mixing valves are working on hand sinks so that they can be  properly used for hand washing. Measures are being taken to address the Issue immediately.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Observed that the rolling carts to transport product out to display shelves have some build up of grease on the sides and wheels. 
Clean these carts.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed some ice build up on the floor of the walk in freezer, at the doorway.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.
Clean the floors.
CORRECTED= ice was scraped off of the floor during the inspection.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean.
Observed some litter/packaging debris in the walk in  cooler.
Clean the floors.
CORRECTED=Debris was cleaned up during inspection.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a hose in the 3 compartment sink in the deli area, that had a split in the side. This hose leads from the sanitizing solution reservoir to the 3rd compartment. The split in the hose was causing the solution to leak out of the hose.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.
Repair the hose.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Bread was observed uncovered in the meat walkin cooler - bag was not properly closed to cover product. Manager had deli staff discard all bread that was in the top portion of the storage bag. The bag was then closed to keep remaining bread covered/protected from potential contamination. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) tracks of deli cases; B) table in meat walkin; C) lower shelf of small table across from hot holding case; & D) tracks/outer ledges of storage areas in hot cases and cabinets below prep tables. Clean general surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1280 - Jacket was observed hanging on a cart next to bags of single service containers. Jacket was moved to proper storage area. An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from food preparation/storage areas and all food related items (i.e. clean equipment, single service items, etc.) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Foods in hot holding case at deli were 93F-135F (gravy, fried potatoes, mashed potatoes, mac-n-cheese, cheese sticks, ravioli, & jalapeno poppers). All foods were discarded in the trash. Hot foods shall be held at 135F/above at all times except during the cooling process. Store hot foods at 135F/above.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.150 - Hot holding case at deli was not holding cooked foods at 135F/above (see #3a above). Quarts lights on top of holding unit were not turned on. Manager thought it may have switched off if a fuse was tripped. Once the quartz lights were turned back on the unit was immediately hotter. New foods were placed in the unit, and everything was at 140F/above. All hot storage units used for potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain product at 135F/above at all times.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Fried chicken cooling on the top of roll cart in the deli walkin cooler was not protected from potential overhead contamination. Place a clean baking sheet or another appropriate item above food items cooling on the top of roll carts. Foods shall be protected at all times.
